findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the emit-compare rule: the plan proposes normalizing BOTH sides at outbound_field_diff.py:292 / outbound_fields.py:564 to cancel lossy artifacts, but those sites deliberately compare the RAW remote to force the once-only stale-body upgrade re-emit — specify how a genuinely-stale body still upgrades exactly once AND a lossy DC round-trip still converges.
evidence: Existing code comment at outbound_field_diff.py:287-291: 'The REMOTE value is deliberately compared RAW … routing it through the port too would make it match the normalized local value, so a stale description would never be rewritten. Comparing raw re-emits it once…'
Identical rationale at outbound_fields.py:555-561: 'The REMOTE value is deliberately NOT normalized here … normalizing it too would make it compare equal … so the differ would never rewrite it…'

Plan asserts BOTH: step 3 'routes the description comparisons … through the codec normalize_outbound so BOTH sides are compared in the same rendered-then-decoded space' AND (cutover section) 'Each already-synced description re-emits exactly once … to upgrade to rich ADF, then converges.'
findings.finding: The emit-compare change (route the REMOTE through normalize_outbound at outbound_field_diff.py:292 / outbound_fields.py:564) contradicts the same sites' existing, load-bearing design of comparing a normalized LOCAL against a RAW REMOTE to force the once-only stale-body upgrade re-emit.
scenarios: A description whose stored wire was written by the OLD plain/identity encoder: normalizing the remote at the emit compare makes it match the fitted local, so the one-time rich upgrade re-emit never fires and the stale body is never upgraded.
For DC's lossy render, comparing the remote RAW re-emits every pass (the problem the plan correctly identifies) — so neither raw nor normalized-both-sides satisfies both requirements as stated.
findings.suggested_fix: Separate the two compares explicitly: keep a raw-remote 'stale/legacy body' detection that forces the one-time upgrade, and add a decode-normalized 'already-rich, lossy-cancel' compare that suppresses subsequent re-emits — and state, per site, which predicate gates emission after cutover.

`_issues.py:40`: `_DESCRIPTION_CODEC = WikiTextCodec()`; `_issues.py:111`: `fields["description"] = _DESCRIPTION_CODEC.fit_outbound(description)`; `_issues.py:162`: `fields = _translate_create_fields(ticket_data)` inside `create_issue` — a second, independent WikiTextCodec() create-path consumer applying `fit_outbound` only, not surfaced in the plan's inventory.
findings.finding: The DC create-path codec-consumer inventory names only `_map_local_to_dc_fields` (backend.py:70), but a second independent `WikiTextCodec()` create-path consumer — `_DESCRIPTION_CODEC` (`_issues.py:40`) used inside `_translate_create_fields` (`_issues.py:93`, line 111), the function the transport's real `create_issue` (`_issues.py:162`) runs — is omitted. It applies `fit_outbound` ONLY; since the plan redefines `to_wire`/`normalize_outbound` (not `fit_outbound`) and patches only `_map_local_to_dc_fields`, this omitted site never renders on create.
findings.location: Scope: `adapters/jira_datacenter/backend.py` (`:70`) — DC CREATE-path: change `_map_local_to_dc_fields`; and 'The DC CREATE path is a SEPARATE, explicitly-enumerated codec consumer: `_map_local_to_dc_fields` (`backend.py:70`) constructs its OWN `WikiTextCodec()`'
scenarios: `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira_datacenter/_issues.py:111` — `_translate_create_fields` calls `_DESCRIPTION_CODEC.fit_outbound(description)` with `_DESCRIPTION_CODEC = WikiTextCodec()` (`:40`); a description reaching `create_issue` (`:162`) through this path is fit but NOT rendered, so a newly-created DC issue ships raw Markdown, defeating the AC 'issue.update/create receives rendered wiki'.

`tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_dc_create_field_translation_18a5.py:285` (`test_the_description_survives_the_translation`) pins `_translate_create_fields`' description output; it is an affected test file the plan's test inventory omits and would break/need updating under the cutover.
findings.suggested_fix: In the DC create-path change, render before the fit in BOTH create writers: `_map_local_to_dc_fields` (backend.py:70) AND `_translate_create_fields` (`_issues.py:111`, whose `_DESCRIPTION_CODEC = WikiTextCodec()` at `:40` today applies only `fit_outbound`), and update `test_dc_create_field_translation_18a5.py`'s description-survival pin to the rendering behavior.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the idempotence requirement explicitly (normalize_outbound(normalize_outbound(x))==normalize_outbound(x)), distinguish it from the codec law, and specify how the ~0.35% non-idempotent DC bodies are prevented from re-emitting every pass (e.g. gate re-emit on the stored rich_sha rather than the text compare).
evidence: Plan: 'guaranteed by the codec law normalize_outbound(t) == decode_inbound(to_wire(t)) … plus the empirically-proven round-trip idempotence (marklas 99.65%).'
Codec-law test test_rich_text_codec.py:163-174 asserts normalize==decode∘to_wire — NOT normalize(normalize(x))==normalize(x).
Plan step 3: 'through the codec normalize_outbound (decode∘to_wire, idempotent by the codec law)' — treats the codec law as if it implied idempotence.
findings.finding: The 'converges exactly once' guarantee for the lossy DC codec relies on normalize_outbound being idempotent, but the plan only establishes the codec LAW (normalize==decode∘to_wire), not idempotence, and its own cited evidence (99.65% round-trip idempotence) implies a ~0.35% non-convergent tail that would re-emit every pass.
findings.location: Prior art bullet 3 and Approach steps 1 & 3
scenarios: A DC description body in the 0.35% that does not round-trip idempotently: normalize_outbound(normalize_outbound(x)) != normalize_outbound(x), so the fitted local and the stored-then-decoded baseline never stabilize and the differ re-emits a description update every pass.
findings.suggested_fix: Add an idempotence pin test for the rendering codec over the marklas corpus and, for bodies that fail it, gate outbound emission on the change-gated rich_sha (wire actually changed) instead of the decode-normalized text compare, so a non-idempotent body still converges after one push.
